cosy-lesson.title: "Do you think so, or were you told to think so?": Anonymous

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Influence – the capacity or power to have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of someone.

p.em: Example: Social media algorithms have a massive influence on the opinions of young teenagers.

cosy-blockquote.p: Independent – free from outside control; capable of thinking, deciding, and acting entirely on one's own.

p.em: Example: Feynman argued that an independent thinker is highly valuable in a world of standardized education.

cosy-blockquote.p: Opinion – a view, belief, or judgment formed about something, not necessarily based on objective fact.

p.em: Example: In a polarized environment, people often mistake a strong personal opinion for absolute truth.

cosy-blockquote.p: To shape – to strongly influence, form, or determine the development of a person's beliefs and thoughts.

p.em: Example: Our parents and childhood environments do a lot to shape our core ethical values.

cosy-blockquote.p: Propaganda – biased, misleading, or highly emotional information used to promote a specific political point of view.

p.em: Example: Strict governments use media propaganda to prevent citizens from thinking independently.

cosy-blockquote.p: Critical – expressing analytical, objective, and reasoned judgments regarding facts, data, or opinions.

p.em: Example: Developing a critical mind is indispensable if you want to detect biases in daily news feeds.

cosy-blockquote.p: Conditioning – the process of training, habituating, or influencing a person to behave and think in a certain way.

p.em: Example: Many of our consumer choices are the result of continuous, subtle social conditioning.

cosy-blockquote.p: Authority – the official power or right to give orders, enforce obedience, or make rules.

p.em: Example: A nonconformist learner refuses to accept ideas simply because they are declared by an authority.

cosy-blockquote.p: To conform – to adjust your behavior, views, or lifestyle to match the accepted standards of a social group.

p.em: Example: The pressure to conform makes it difficult for individuals to express their original, unorthodox thoughts.

cosy-blockquote.p: To question – to feel or express doubt about something; to challenge an established assumption or dogma.

p.em: Example: It is our duty as active learners to question everything we read on the internet.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
What does this quote teach us about our daily opinion and where it comes from?
★ It is believed that independent thinkers shape society. How is critical thinking encouraged in your environment?

How does the continuous influence of advertisements affect our consumer habits?
★ Do you consider yourself highly independent when making major career decisions?

How do modern social media feeds do so much to shape our political views?
★ Can you name one value that your parents did a lot to shape in your mind?

Why do people so easily fall for propaganda during times of global crisis?
★ Do you actively use critical thinking when reading shocking online headlines?

How does childhood social conditioning prevent us from discovering our authentic identity?
★ What is one childhood rule or expectation that you chose to question as an adult?

Why is it important to challenge the rigid boundaries set by traditional authority?
★ Have you ever had to choose between showing quiet loyalty and staying true to your own truth?

Why is the pressure to conform to group thinking so intense in corporate workplaces?
★ Do you usually feel a pressure to conform, or are you highly comfortable staying unique?

How does an active, critical mind protect us from falling for comfortable illusions?
★ What is the most important question we should ask when we have a strong doubt?

Why is it vital for our personal freedom to continuously to question what we are told?
★ Do you find it easy to admit your ignorance when discussing complex subjects with experts?

If you could change one aspect of your childhood conditioning, what would it be?
★ If you had to describe your relationship with independent thought in one word, what would it be?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: Discuss with your partner: In which scenario is it most difficult to think independently and resist social conditioning? Rank them: - 🏢 Corporate Meetings When your boss and colleagues all share an opinion that you believe is completely wrong. - 🌐 Digital Timelines When social media algorithms continuously flood your feed with highly emotional, biased news. - 🏡 Family Traditions When your parents' traditional values and expectations clash directly with your unorthodox choices. - 👥 Core Friendship Circles When you must hide your authentic views to stay accepted and avoid conflict in your close social group.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, digital neural networks will scan our brains to identify and erase all our hidden social conditioning. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you allow a machine to optimize your mind by clearing your biases?

As information becomes even more overwhelming, future societies will retreat into extreme dogmatism to survive. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Should schools teach children how to detect propaganda in media from a young age?

Future artificial intelligence will display such perfect, unbiased logic that human authority will look arrogant in comparison. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Could you trust an AI judge to make perfectly objective decisions?

Our future reliance on algorithms will create a world of comfortable ignorance, where humans no longer question anything. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If technology managed everything, would you mind being ignorant of how it functions?

In the coming decades, choosing not to conform and thinking independently will be highly rewarded. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you fear a future where your personal opinion is monitored by online scores?

Future search engines will answer questions instantly, rendering active human critical inquiry obsolete. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you miss the joy of searching for answers if everything were known instantly?

In the coming decades, virtual reality spaces will allow perfectly unbiased dialogue between historical enemies. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you participate in a global digital dialogue with strangers to solve world issues?

Future bio-engineering will allow us to physically upgrade human empathy, turning honesty into a biological guarantee rather than a choice. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you take a pill that guaranteed you would always act with perfect honesty?

We will eventually wear wearable sensors that make us dynamically aware of when we are being influenced by others. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you wear a wristband that vibrated whenever you showed dogmatic thinking?

The hyper-accelerated future will leave absolutely no time to quietly contemplate the truth of our existence. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If life became twice as fast, how would you preserve your mental peace?

ul.li: Incorrect: I studies in an independent way → Correct: I study in an independent manner ((First-person verb agreement, use 'manner' to match original quote))
Incorrect: He discussed about the opinion → Correct: He discussed the opinion (('Discuss' is transitive and does not take 'about'))
Incorrect: I am agree with Feynman → Correct: I agree with Feynman (('Agree' is a verb, not an adjective))
